content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble and could use some help. I watched a tutorial on YouTube about connecting and configuring a temperature sensor to [product_name]. My module displays a value of 100 degrees, but the actual temperature should be around 20-23 degrees. Is my wiring incorrect? I have +24VDC on the top (blue and red wires), with the white wire going directly to I7. The other two wires connect to the PT1000 sensor. Currently, I measure 12.8 volts at my I7 input. I expected the transmitter to output 0-10 volts. Attached are some pictures.
I'm using a [product_name] with article number [article_no]. I've also attached the configuration for the analog input settings.

The lower row of terminals on the left provides the 0-10V output for I7. The sensor should be connected to the middle and right terminals. Based on your photo, it looks like the sensor is connected to the left and middle terminals instead.

Hi, I've made the changes you suggested. Now I have two PT1000 sensors connected—one measuring about 20–22 degrees (outside temperature), and another in the freezer showing -15–18 degrees, which is connected to input 1 (AI3). I'm getting readings of 13.4 volts (outside) and 12.4 volts (freezer). There's a difference, but the voltages seem too high.

Are you using the same power supply for both the sensor and the [product_name]? You mentioned PT1000, but it appears your transmitter is compatible only with PT100 sensors, not PT1000. Voltages above 10V are not acceptable.
Yes, I'm using the same 24VDC power supply—specifically, [company_name] SITOP.
Are there PT1000 transmitters like the ones you described? Do you think I need a different transmitter (the blue box)?

I also have a blue box transmitter from China made for PT100 sensors. When I connect a PT100 sensor, the voltage range is correct. If I swap the PT100 for a 1000 Ohm resistor, the voltage jumps to 12.8V. You need either a PT1000-compatible transmitter or PT100 thermal resistors.
Thank you for clarifying. I will order PT100 sensors to resolve this. I couldn't find any PT1000-compatible transmitters.
There are PT1000 transmitters available, but not the blue box models from China.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue discussed is the discrepancy between the temperature readings on the [product_name] module and actual temperatures, due to incompatible sensor and transmitter pairings (PT1000 sensor with PT100 transmitter). Users also encountered difficulties with analog input wiring and the need to keep voltage within the 0–10V range. The thread highlights general confusion among users about selecting the correct sensors and transmitters for [product_name] modules, as well as the challenge of finding compatible PT1000 transmitters.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants their temperature sensors and transmitter to show accurate measurements (~20–23°C and –15–18°C) on the [product_name], with analog input voltages kept within the 0–10V specification.
